span.p:
Clients
external zones: Traffic Manager picks the cell by DNS
internal clients: straight to the gateway

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 360px; text-align: center; width: 360px;

span.p:
Certificate renewal job of the environment
managed identity, Officer roles on the platform vault only
DNS-01 · once a month, one certificate at a time

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 360px; text-align: center; width: 360px;

span.p:
Let's Encrypt (ACME, DNS-01)
the _acme-challenge TXT records go into a public validation zone,
nothing else is public

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 360px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Platform Key Vault of the exposure
one wildcard certificate per isolation zone,
e.g. *.int-fi.<env>.example.com

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 360px; text-align: center; width: 360px;

span.p:
Zone gateway (Traefik): one HTTPS listener on 443
HTTP/2 and TLS 1.3 only · certificate Secret written by ESO
no port 80: Azure Policy denies HTTP listeners

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 360px; text-align: center;

span.p:
app-a pods on nodes A and B
h2c (HTTP/2 cleartext), no TLS in the application

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 360px; text-align: center;

span.p: Internal load balancer Service, port 443 only

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 360px; text-align: center;

span.p:
app-x pod terminates TLS itself
the zone certificate as PEM files (ESO Secret)
